title: On Drawing the plan on one sheet
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：draw　|　正文 351 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 draw 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the elder ① drew the plan on one sheet with great care, and every youth in the village said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the elder ② draws the plan on one sheet on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ draw the plan on one sheet at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ drawn the plan on one sheet before — a line in the memoir for November 1970 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Drawing the plan on one sheet with great care, the elder said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far gate, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ draw the curtains against the sun on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Draw the curtains against the sun at once and never mention it again.

By 1983 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the memoir, and a new youth from the next village ⑧ draws the curtains against the sun with great care every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the gate, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ drew the plan on one sheet again when nobody else would.

⑩ To draw the plan on one sheet, my mother said in 1988, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the village remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the village forgets, somebody draws the plan on one sheet on the same day again and somebody must draw the plan on one sheet with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 画出（一般过去式 drew the plan on one sheet：1976 年长者头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 画出（一般现在 draws the plan on one sheet：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 画出（不定式 to draw the plan on one sheet：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 画出（过去完成时 had drawn the plan on one sheet：1970 年十一月的回忆录上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 画出（动名词 drawing the plan on one sheet 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 拉（帘）（draw the curtains against the sun：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去拉（帘）把帘子拉上挡太阳）
G. v. 拉（帘）（draw the curtains against the sun：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 画出（后段两处：新来的后生照例 draws the curtains against the sun，而母亲又一次 drew the plan on one sheet）

answers.why: draw 意为“画出”，1976 年长者小心翼翼地画出在一张纸上画出那张图样，那是村子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 drew。
draw 意为“画出”，自那以后长者当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 draws。
draw 意为“画出”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯画出在一张纸上画出那张图样”，此处为不定式 to draw the plan on one sheet。
draw 意为“画出”，回忆录里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1983 年之前就有人画出过，故用过去完成时 had drawn。
draw 意为“画出”，长者说“画出在一张纸上画出那张图样这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 drawing the plan on one sheet 作主语。
draw 意为“拉（帘）”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去拉（帘）把帘子拉上挡太阳”，should ever 之后用原形 draw the curtains against the sun。
draw 意为“拉（帘）”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻拉（帘）把帘子拉上挡太阳（draw the curtains against the sun at once），以后再也不要提起。
draw 意为“画出”，新来的后生每个年头都照例拉（帘）把帘子拉上挡太阳，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 draws。
draw 意为“画出”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地画出在一张纸上画出那张图样，用一般过去式 drew 叙述。
draw 意为“画出”，结尾那句是母亲 1988 年的话：要画出在一张纸上画出那张图样，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和村子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 draw 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1976 the elder drew the plan on one sheet with great care, and nobody in the village forgot it.
Even now the elder draws the plan on one sheet on the same day whenever the village asks.
Drawing the plan on one sheet with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever draw the curtains against the sun on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new youth from the next village draws the curtains against the sun with great care every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother drew the plan on one sheet again, and the village remembered that half.
